Subject: ACME - Model routing & policy configuration (post-call recap)

Hi Sarah / Tom -

Thanks again for taking time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side so we stay aligned on integration & policy requirements: 

Summary from call:
- Primary goals: route user queries to the lowest-cost compatible model while meeting a 200ms p99 latency SLO for chat flows; fall back to higher-capacity models for long-context summarization.
- Security: ACME will use customer-managed keys (KMS) and wants private deployment option for PII workloads.
- Integration surface: SDK + server-side routing (preferably a stateless proxy) + embeddings for similarity/reranking.

Action items we agreed to:
1) Redwood to share a short integration checklist (SDK snippets, auth tokens, example routing policy).
2) ACME to share representative prompt patterns and expected QPS for chat vs. batch rerank.
3) Technical deep-dive with Dev + Marcus for SDK auth & routing logic (target next week).

Attachments: I attached a 1-pager with a recommended model-routing policy and a simple architecture diagram.

Notes on our proposed model-routing policy (high-level):
- Route by intent/latency class: quick-chat -> lower-cost quantized Llama-variant on regional hosts; long-context/hallucination-sensitive -> higher-precision model.
- Cost floor: enable cost-based thresholds so non-critical queries default to cheaper model if cost per token exceeds threshold X.
- Fallback chain: preferred model -> regional replica -> cheaper variant -> queued/async rerank (for non-interactive workloads).
- Region routing: prioritize US-east for lowest latency with automatic failover to US-west / EU as configured by customer.

Please let us know if anything above needs correction. Dev and Marcus - can you prepare the SDK auth snippet + a suggested JSON routing policy we can share with ACME before the deep-dive?

Best,

Hi Sarah - good questions. Quick technical notes addressing your point about a "cheap estimate" step and some SDK/auth details we can share: 

1) Preflight estimator:
- We commonly provide a zero-shot estimator route that runs a tiny tokenizer/complexity model (100ms median) to estimate token count + classification into latency buckets. This can be configured as a preflight policy and priced at a discounted unit cost.
- Implementation: lightweight RPC that returns {"estimated_tokens": <n>, "latency_class": "fast|normal|slow"}. For interactive flows you can run it synchronously; for batch reranks you can run it as an offline pass.

2) SDK + auth snippets (high-level):
- Short-lived bearer tokens for POC (rotate every 1 hour).
- For production: we recommend KMS-backed signing for tokens and mutual TLS for private deployments.
- Example header: Authorization: Bearer <short-lived-token>
- If using private deployment behind your VPC, we can exchange a service account + signed JWT.

3) Routing policy (suggested JSON keys):
- priority: ["latency", "cost", "quality"]
- routes: [{match: {intent: "chat"}, model_pool: "low_cost_quant", max_latency_ms: 200}, {match: {intent: "summarize"}, model_pool: "high_quality_long_context", max_latency_ms: 2000}]
- fallbacks: ["regional_replica", "cheaper_variant", "async_queue"]
- region_preference: ["us-east-1", "us-west-2"]

We're attaching a quick sample snippet and a reference route file - happy to walk through in the deep-dive.

Marcus
